From 2bf2d65f76697820dbc4227d13866293576dd90a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Junrui Luo <moonafterrain@outlook.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 23:42:58 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: target: core: Fix integer overflow in UNMAP bounds
 check

sbc_execute_unmap() checks LBA + range does not exceed the device capacity,
but does not guard against LBA + range wrapping around on 64-bit overflow.

Add an overflow check matching the pattern already used for WRITE_SAME in
the same file.

Fixes: 86d7182985d2 ("target: Add sbc_execute_unmap() helper")
Reported-by: Yuhao Jiang <danisjiang@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Junrui Luo <moonafterrain@outlook.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/SYBPR01MB7881593C61AD52C69FBDB0BDAF7CA@SYBPR01MB7881.ausprd01.prod.outlook.com
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

diff --git a/drivers/target/target_core_sbc.c b/drivers/target/target_core_sbc.c
index abe91dc8722e..21f5cb86d70c 100644
--- a/drivers/target/target_core_sbc.c
+++ b/drivers/target/target_core_sbc.c
@@ -1187,7 +1187,8 @@ sbc_execute_unmap(struct se_cmd *cmd)
 			goto err;
 		}
 
-		if (lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1) {
+		if (lba + range < lba ||
+		    lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1) {
 			ret = TCM_ADDRESS_OUT_OF_RANGE;
 			goto err;
 		}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Modifications in Each File

- **`drivers/target/target_core_sbc.c`** (in `sbc_execute_unmap()` function)  
  Added an integer overflow check before the existing bounds check for UNMAP operations. The original condition:
  ```c
  if (lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1)
  ```
  was replaced with:
  ```c
  if (lba + range < lba ||
      lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1)
  ```

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The added `lba + range < lba` condition detects when `lba + range` wraps around due to a 64-bit overflow. Without this guard, a malicious or erroneous UNMAP command could bypass the device capacity bounds check by intentionally overflowing the sum, potentially causing out-of-range operations. The fix aligns with the overflow prevention pattern already used for the `WRITE_SAME` command in the same file, ensuring consistent safety across similar operations.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1)
Reason:
The addition `lba + range` is performed without checking for integer overflow. If `lba` and `range` are large enough, the sum can wrap around to a small value, allowing the check to pass even when the actual (unwrapped) range exceeds the device capacity.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (lba + range < lba ||
    lba + range > dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1)
Reason:
The condition `lba + range < lba` detects an overflow by checking whether the sum is less than one of the operands. When overflow occurs, the sum wraps to a smaller value, triggering this check and returning a correct out-of-range error. If no overflow occurs, the original capacity check is applied as intended.
